title.narrative: Skills for Future Economy Sector Development Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The sector development program (SDP) is part of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) support to the Government of Cambodia to strengthen human capital and transform the country into a technology-driven, knowledge-based industrial economy. It combines a programmatic PBL approach with a project investment to achieve strategically sequenced structural and institutional reforms in technical and vocational education and training (TVET), which includes increased private sector involvement to address skills gaps and shortages. The SDP will improve employability of the current and future labor force through policy reforms and project investments that will mutually reinforce each other to enhance the skills development ecosystem, deliver industry-led inclusive training, and mobilize more resources for demand-driven skills development.

Output: Industry-led inclusive skills training delivered Indicator: A partnership agreement to operationalize skills training in the T&A ITM signed between the MEF and TAFTAC Progress/Status: The Partnership Agreement to operationalize skills training in the T&A ITM was signed between the MEF and TAFTAC 27 March 2023.
At end of June 2026, 6 training proposals were awarded, covering 43 skills, 12,380 trainees (f = 5,934 or 48%).
Of the 6 training proposals awarded, 11,162 trainees (f = 7,423 trainees or 67%) completed the courses while the trainings are still ongoing.
- The training progress reaches 74% of the 15,000 target trainees. Data Source: Signed agreement Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: not applicable Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: not applicable Target year: 2023 Target value: signed

Output: Industry-led inclusive skills training delivered Indicator: Gender-responsive and inclusive skills framework for the T&A industry developed Progress/Status: Firm to support TAFTAC to skills framework has been mobilized.
T & Skills Framework has been developed and completed.
At least 50% of TAFTAC companies introduced “lean thinking, 5S, and SEAH training for employees” Data Source: SDF records from TAFTAC Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: not applicable Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: not applicable Target year: 2030 Target value: developed

Output: Industry-led inclusive skills training delivered Indicator: New investment law incentivizing skills development and adoption of technology Progress/Status: - On June 26, 2023, the Cambodian Royal Government approved Sub-Decree No. 139 ANKr. BK concerning the Execution of the Investment Law ("Sub-Decree").
The objective is to put into effect the stipulations of the Investment Law enacted on October 15, 2021 ("Investment Law"). Data Source: Promulgated investment law Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: law promulgated Baseline year: 2021 Baseline value: law promulgated Target year: 2023 Target value: law enacted

Output: Industry-led inclusive skills training delivered Indicator: TAFTAC companies introduced “lean thinking,” 5S, and SEAH training for employees Achievement: 13% Progress/Status: - The signed Annual Training Plan 2025 includes Green, 5S, and lean thinking modules for upskilling.
5,090 (f = 3,366 or 66%) have completed the skills training courses on SEAH, 5S (Green 5S), Lean thinking (Lean thinking, Lean 5S Kaized and Lean management) for 93 companies that are members of TAFTAC or 14% of the 674 members of TAFTAC.
- Compared to the target of 50% of TAFTAC members (337 companies), the project now reaches 28%.
- Following TAFTAC's endorsement of the new Skills Framework, SDF will strengthen collaboration with TAFTAC and its member companies to facilitate the preparation and submission of Joint Training Proposals (JTPs) in the next quarter.
- SDF will strengthen outreach and engagement activities with TAFTAC to promote demand-driven skills development and encourage greater private sector investment in workforce training. Data Source: SDF records from TAFTAC Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: not applicable Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: not applicable Target year: 2030 Target value: at least 50% Actual value: 13%

Output: Industry-led inclusive skills training delivered Indicator: The ITM for T&A industry approved and implementation started by MEF Progress/Status: - The Industry Transformation Map (ITM) for the Textiles and Apparel (T&A) sector approved by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) on 17 March 2023.
- MEF has signed a partnership agreement with TAFTAC as a part of ITM implementation, specifically to strengthen private sector engagement & partnership, enhance human resources through skills development, and promote technology adoption.
- Following revisions to the T&A Skills Framework in response to ADB's feedback on skills development, TAFTAC and SDF jointly approved the T&A Skills Framework on 24 March 2026. Data Source: MEF policy on ITM of T&A Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: drafted Baseline year: 2022 Baseline value: drafted Target year: 2023 Target value: approved
